**Åben kirurgi** (open surgery) is a primary medical procedure and one of the two main surgical methods tracked and benchmarked in the Danish healthcare system. Within the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (Acute Surgery Database), it is systematically quantified and compared against minimally invasive (closed) surgery to evaluate treatment patterns across Denmark [^src1]. 

The database, published by the Danish Healthcare Quality Institute (Sundhedsvæsenets Kvalitetsinstitut) on February 28, 2025, utilizes these metrics as quality measures and benchmarking tools for regional healthcare authorities [^src1]. The analyses focus on the age distribution of operated patients and the regional and institutional distribution of surgical methods over three reporting periods, spanning from 2021 to 2024 [^src1]. These insights are designed to support both political and clinical decision-making regarding the development of surgical practices [^src1].

While earlier sections of the 2024 report provide quantitative tables comparing the two methods, page 81 specifically introduces a supplementary graph dedicated to tracking the temporal development of "åben kirurgi" at the regional level [^src1]. This analytical expansion builds upon the previous quantitative data, though the specific visual graph and its underlying data points are not detailed in the immediate text of this document chunk [^src1].
